title: Musical rhythm spectra from Bach to Joplin obey a 1/f power law
read: main text in full; supplement not reached
verdict: Notated rhythm across 1,788 classical movements is 1/f-like (median beta 0.78); order, not the durations themselves, makes it; composers differ more in rhythm than pitch. Says nothing about quality.

title: Statistical learning and probabilistic prediction in music cognition: mechanisms of stylistic enculturation
read: in full (author's copy)
verdict: IDyOM's information content predicts pitch expectation (up to 83% of variance), memory, similarity, boundaries; unpredictable passages lower valence; inverted U unresolved; no quality score.

title: Anatomically distinct dopamine release during anticipation and experience of peak emotion to music
read: in full (lab's copy)
verdict: Chills music releases striatal dopamine; caudate rises in the ~15 s before the peak, nucleus accumbens at the peak; 8-10 young adults, self-chosen music; does not name the musical structure that drives anticipation.

title: Commonality and variation in mental representations of music revealed by a cross-cultural comparison of rhythm priors in 15 countries
read: main text and first part of methods (first 100,000 of 265,000 characters); later methods and supplement not reached
verdict: 39 groups, 15 countries: every group's rhythm prior peaks at small-integer ratios (1:1:1, 1:1:2 everywhere); emphasis on others (3:3:2, 2:2:3, 7:2:3) follows local music. Follows Jacoby & McDermott 2017 (not read: paywalled).

title: Preferences for consonance are evident in Indigenous Amazonians with higher, but not lower, levels of global integration
authors: McPherson, Undurraga, Dolan, Durango, Medina, Godoy, McDermott
read: in full (lab's copy); revisits McDermott et al. 2016 (not read: paywalled)
verdict: Less-integrated Tsimane' show no consonance preference; more-integrated show a small one; everyone dislikes roughness. Consonance preference is at least partly learned; roughness aversion looks shared.

title: Uncertainty and surprise jointly predict musical pleasure and amygdala, hippocampus, and auditory cortex activity
authors: Cheung, Harrison, Meyer, Pearce, Haynes, Koelsch
read: main text, STAR methods and references in full (author's copy + publisher HTML); supplement not reached (fetch blocked)
verdict: Surprise x uncertainty predicts first-hearing pleasure of 30 chord progressions (39 raters; fMRI replication in 40); surprise mostly lowers pleasure; no held-out test; says nothing direct about lasting love or covers.

title: Predicting variation of folk songs: a corpus analysis study on the memorability of melodies
read: article in full (UvA repository copy); supplement not reached (fetch blocked)
verdict: Short, early, low-surprise, small-interval phrases survive Dutch oral transmission better (9,639 phrases, 147 tune families); notes explain ~5% (marginal R2); no held-out test; faithful copying, not choosing to perform.

title: Experimental study of inequality and unpredictability in an artificial cultural market
read: article and supporting online material in full (author copies)
verdict: Social influence makes success of 48 unknown songs more unequal and unpredictable (14,341 participants, 8 social worlds); quality is a listener measure; caps note-based prediction to the tails; silent on decades of love.

title: Assessing the impact of sampling, remixes, and covers on original song popularity
read: v1 HTML in full (short workshop paper, no supplement)
verdict: Borrowings (mostly samples) sometimes lift search interest in the original; 884 pairs, no controls or multiple-test correction, counts don't reconcile, covers not separated; hints covers feed back into lasting love.

title: Cover versions as an impact indicator in popular music: A quantitative network analysis
read: article in full (Semantic Scholar PDF mirror); supporting files S1, S2 and S1 Fig not reached
verdict: Artist-level SecondHandSongs network (106k artists, 855k covers): covers very unequal (top 100 take 41%), mostly within genre (jazz 73%); no songs, no notes, no tests. Cover counts partly measure fame and genre.

title: Population Ecology of Tunes
read: arXiv HTML v1 in full; supplementary material not available anywhere
verdict: 22,216 Irish tunes, 820,752 tunebook adds: real per-tune fitness, weak conformity; held-out R2 0.29, prestige ~16 points, melody ~3; simpler tunes spread a little better. No harmony, no replication.

title: Repeated listening increases the liking for music regardless of its complexity: implications for the appreciation and aesthetics of music
read: PMC HTML in full; figures and track-list supplement not reached
verdict: 15 listeners, 40 unknown instrumental excerpts, 28 hearings: liking rises at every complexity level (rated from audio), no interaction, no inverted U; simpler pieces rated duller. Small, no control group.

title: Decoding the evolution of melodic and harmonic structure of Western music through the lens of network science
authors: Di Marco, Loru, Galeazzi, Cinelli, Quattrociocchi
read: arXiv preprint PDF and published open-access PDF (Sapienza repository) in full; published Supplementary Information not reached
verdict: ~21,000 MIDI files, note-transition networks: classical and jazz more complex, genres simplifying over time; only outcome is Spotify popularity (preprint), |r| < 0.07 in pop and rock. Method useful, no greatness signal.

title: Ricci curvature of Markov chains on metric spaces
read: arXiv v4 PDF in full via a summarising reader (all sections, items 1-51, bibliography); card_1.md
verdict: Coarse Ricci curvature of any random walk; positive curvature forces spectral gap >= min kappa (Prop. 29), contraction, concentration. Tested tonight as move-weighted lazy curvature of the chord walk: killed (-0.0002 within artist; power 0.06). On tiny chord maps curvature tracks size.

title: Discrete curvature on graphs from the effective resistance
read: arXiv v3 PDF in full incl. appendices A-F and bibliography; card_2.md
verdict: Resistance curvature; bridges are links with c*omega = 1; mean node curvature is 1/n. Bridge indicator tested tonight: killed (+0.021 against -0.025 predicted).

title: The Torii of Phases
venue: Mathematics and Computation in Music, LNCS 7937
read: arXiv HTML v1 in full incl. footnotes and references; card_1.md
verdict: Chords as points on the (phi3, phi5) Fourier-phase torus; Lemma 2 (transposition shifts phases) proved. P/L/R share and thirds axis tested: both killed (power 0.07-0.08); winding/area undefined on pop loops (whole-step same-quality moves are half-turns in phi3).

title: Discogs-VI: A Musical Version Identification Dataset Based on Public Editorial Metadata
authors: R. Oguz Araz, Xavier Serra, Dmitry Bogdanov
read: arXiv PDF v1 in full (no appendix); card_2.md; HTML, Zenodo and GitHub READMEs not reached
verdict: Cliques = exact normalised title + shared Written-By credit; >= 2 performer sets; single-version songs excluded; no error audit. Basis for tonight's new outcome (in Discogs-VI at all).

title: Topological Periodicity Test (TopPT) via Confidence Bound of Time-Delay Embeddings
authors: Donghyun Park, Junhyun An, Taehyoung Kim, Jisu Kim
read: arXiv HTML v4 in full (sections 1-8, appendices A-I, references), via a paraphrasing fetch tool; card_1.md
verdict: Proves the sliding-window cloud of a smooth periodic signal is an embedded circle with one early H1 bar of guaranteed persistence, non-periodic gives none; subsampling radius gives a test with error control. Basis of run05 loop_margin (killed).

title: Musical trends and predictability of success in contemporary songs in and out of the top charts
authors: Myra Interiano, Kamyar Kazemi, Lijia Wang, Jienian Yang, Zhaoxia Yu, Natalia L. Komarova
read: UC eScholarship PDF copy in full (methods, results, discussion, captions, Table 1, references); supplement not reached; card_2.md
verdict: Counter-evidence: audio descriptors 0.69-0.75 accuracy on chart entry; adding an artist superstar flag 0.82-0.86. Sound not notes; chart entry not longevity or covers. Motivated run05 fame_vs_notes (killed; proxy broken).

title: Helmholtz-Hodge Decomposition on Graphs
read: arXiv HTML in full, five passes; abs page blocked; card_1.md
verdict: Mathematics: three-way orthogonal split of edge fields with no 2-cells; reader found the dimension claims fail beyond single-cycle graphs. Its gradient part on one chord walk is the first-to-last unit current (run06 theorem), so 'downhill' reads clip boundaries; stopped on the notes. Grounded run06 chirality (Green's theorem on the cycle part).

title: Circular Directional Flow Decomposition of Networks
read: arXiv HTML in full, seven passes (sections 1-7, appendices A-G, references); abs page blocked; card_2.md
verdict: Mathematics: balanced/acyclic split of a flow network, non-unique (polytope complex); maximal-circular and BFF splits. On one song it is one start-to-end path plus loops; loop measures mostly count distinct chords (stopped).

title: Hyperbolicity, slimness, and minsize, on average
read: arXiv HTML in full, ten passes; card_1.md
verdict: Average four-point hyperbolicity and four other tree-likeness averages; average delta is bounded by average slimness/minsize, not the reverse. Gave H4m (tree_h4m): killed on 5,901 fresh whole songs.

title: Sliding windows and persistence: an application of topological methods to signal analysis
read: arXiv HTML in full, four passes; card_2.md
verdict: Proved periodicity score from H1 persistence of sliding-window clouds; window-equals-period rule. Ring test withdrawn by its author (noise); the rule shaped loop_period (unsettled).

title: Transportation distances on the circle (and applications)
authors: Julien Rabin, Julie Delon, Yann Gousseau
read: arXiv PDF v3 in full (ar5iv refused unattended); card_1.md
verdict: Closed-form circular W1 (median of CDF differences) and convex costs as a line problem over a shift; gave key travel TRAV5 (killed) and econ (estimate, wrong sign).

title: Turnover rate of popularity charts in neutral models
read: arXiv abstract page full text in five passes (ar5iv refused unattended); card_2.md; Bentley et al. 2007 skimmed for context
verdict: COUNTER-EVIDENCE: content-free copying fits chart turnover. Our timeline test rejected pure copying (slope 0.91, sublinear) and left at most 48% of late-cover spread for content; heritability passed against a within-cell neutral null.

title: A Primer on the Signature Method in Machine Learning
read: arXiv HTML v2 in ten passes, all sections and bibliography; card_1.md
verdict: MATHEMATICS: signatures, Lévy area, Chen, shuffle, lead-lag, uniqueness up to tree-like paths. Five signature/voice-leading measures built from it (TQ, IRR, VR4c, TYP; TR) were estimates under the power floor; none decided anything; IRR came out opposite to its prediction (uncounted).

title: JSIR: An Audio-Aligned, Multi-Task Dataset of Jazz Standard Recordings
read: arXiv HTML and PDF v1; data cloned (github MALerLab/JSIR at 1dd6b8b, CC BY-SA 4.0); card_2.md
verdict: DATA for the obstacle: recordings' ii-V share equals the lead sheets' (0.151-0.155, r 0.99), but lead sheets were built from the recordings and recordings chosen for canonical changes, so weak evidence against performer leakage.

title: Musical Stylistic Analysis: A Study of Intervallic Transition Graphs via Persistent Homology
authors: Martín Mijangos, Alessandro Bravetti, Pablo Padilla
read: arXiv HTML v1, whole paper; card_1.md
verdict: MATHEMATICS (construction only): pitch-class transition graph -> shortest-path metric -> Vietoris-Rips persistence (H0, H1), persistent entropy; no theorems, 18 quartet movements, no statistics. Gave pe_h0 (killed by range, +0.016) and the arch persistence ARCH_PE (unsettled; vanishes with baselines).

title: Contrasting statistical patterns in melodic and molecular evolution reveal distinctive constraints in a culturally evolving system
authors: John M. McBride, W. Tecumseh Fitch
read: arXiv HTML v1, body, supplement 1-8, bibliography (figure images not seen); card_2.md
verdict: COUNTER-EVIDENCE on TheSession itself: across 51,680 aligned version pairs, common pitches, strong beats and small steps are conserved; mutability falls with prevalence (r -0.95). What survives is what is typical, partly by conformity. Gave core_ic (typical melody; passed on A) and the wear-not-cause obstacle.

verdict: maths sound as stated; its room measures (ROOMS, GAP) killed on Hooktheory melodies in run 11
